top_story.headline: Space Command's planned command-and-control facility will require a builder who can post a $2.5 billion bond
top_story.dek: A qualifications form attached to a Defense Department special notice sets a $2.5 billion payment-and-performance bond as the minimum for the design-build contractor.
paragraphs: The U.S. Space Command is seeking a design-build contractor for its Command and Control Facility under a notice titled "Design-Build Contractor (DBC) for Collaborative Delivery," posted under the Department of Defense as a special notice. An attachment, the Minimum Qualifications Form, says the offeror must have "the capacity to provide a project payment and performance bond of a minimum of $2.5 billion (construction value of non-C4IT Work)."

The form is a certification: by submitting it, an offeror attests that each of its minimum-qualification statements is true. The row quoted above is headed "Financial and Bonding Capacity." The form also refers to a "Challenge Statement" and to documentation tying projects to it. The notice carries no price or award estimate in the material reviewed here.
This comes from a file posted October 15 and read for the first time today. The notice's own text did not surface the bonding requirement.

blocks.title: Veterans Affairs gives incumbent Cooper Thomas an urgent three-month medical coding and auditing contract without competition
meta: no amount stated in the material reviewed
Department of Veterans Affairs, Network Contract Office 22
blocks.text: According to the award notice document, which was posted October 15 and read today, the requirement was urgent to keep healthcare documentation and billing moving without disrupting veteran care. The three-month contract was meant to bridge to a proper competition for a new long-term contract. The document says "Cooper Thomas was the only vendor able to meet this requirement because they are the incumbent contractor."

blocks.title: Air Force test center seeks whitepapers to modernize Test Site 2 at its Aerospace Vehicle Survivability Facility at Wright-Patterson
meta: Air Force Materiel Command, Air Force Test Center (Arnold Engineering Development Complex)
blocks.text: The request for whitepapers is aimed at the Arnold Engineering Development Complex's consortium performers and industry partners. It is issued under 10 U.S.C. § 4022 other transaction authority, which sits outside the standard contracting rules. The goal is a test facility able to run Live Fire Test and Evaluation on current and future aerospace systems at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Ohio. The one attachment has not yet been read.

blocks.title: Coast Guard plans to give McClellan Business Park fire protection at its Sacramento air station without competition for up to five years
blocks.text: According to the synopsis, posted October 15 and read today, the contract would run up to five years, with a base period and four option periods. The Coast Guard says that in November 2001 the County of Sacramento and McClellan Business Park LLC signed a 99-year agreement making the company responsible for operating and maintaining the airfield facilities, so it "is the only responsible source capable of meeting the USCG's requirement."

sections.headline: Army signed a $128.9 million Patriot missile production modification and a $23.7 million Patriot adjustment, both just published
paragraphs: From this morning's edition: USAspending.gov is pulled once a day.

USAspending showed 45 new awards of $2 million or more, 31 of them Defense Department awards just published after the 90-day hold, plus 5 large modifications and 6 cuts. Eleven of these actions are featured below. The 45 routine actions are listed, each linked, in 'USAspending: Every Other New Award' at the end of the edition. Defense items below were signed July 17 and published this week; Defense Department contract data is released with a 90-day delay.

blocks.text: Notable awards

Belt Built CFM Joint Venture, LLC won $5,860,944 from the Department of the Army for a firm-fixed-price construction project at the Naval Research Laboratory in Washington, D.C. The classification is repair or alteration of office buildings. It was signed July 17 and published this week. (award)

Black & Veatch Special Projects Corp. received $13,813,157 from the Army, through the Kansas City District of the Army Corps of Engineers, for architect and engineering work. The firm will prepare a design-bid-build request for proposals for a Homeland Defense Over the Horizon Radar project with land acquisition. The description says it is a sole source. It was signed July 17 and published this week. (award)

Windsor Group LLC won $5,498,082 from Washington Headquarters Services for subject matter experts in 'specialized and strategic support services' for the Office of Strategic Capital. The description gives no further detail on the work. It was signed July 17 and published this week. (award)

Continuity Global Solutions LLC received $3,766,735 from the Department of the Air Force for construction security surveillance services supporting secure construction projects. Its performance work statement refers to project B3267 and contract FA520526D007. It was signed July 17 and published this week. (award)
Patriot missile production

Lockheed Martin Corporation had two Army actions on Patriot Advanced Capability-3 missile production, both signed July 17 and published this week. One is a supplemental agreement for work within scope (modification P00079) adding $128,933,590. The other is a definitized letter contract (modification PZ0137) with a net change of −$23,711,189. The description does not say work was reduced, so the negative figure may reflect a pricing settlement rather than a program cut. (+$128.9M modification, −$23.7M modification)
